messages:
incident_bot: PAGER: ARC: arcadia-prod-vpc - /v1/generate errors spike + tail latency 95th > 4s, error rate 6% over 5m, severity P1. incident_bot: Pager details: tenant=arcadia, pool=dedicated-pool-7, model=arcadia-base-2.0. oncall_elena: ACK — jumping in. allocating pager channel. oncall_elena: quick check: is this impacting only ARC tenant or cross-tenant? runtime_dev_jay: initial metrics show errors are 100% from ARC tenant, requests failing in runtime with "KV cache miss fallout" and OOM-ish allocations on replica nodes. ml_lead_sam: likely tokenization edge-case? but kv-cache related points to runtime. runtime_dev_jay: reproducer: small prompt that hits long seq. seeing spikes when clients send 8-10k token contexts. runtime_dev_jay: @oncall_elena can we route ARC to safe variant that has reduced max_context and heavier quant to reduce memory? oncall_elena: yes. steps proposed: 1) pin ARC tenant to safe variant (arcadia-base-2.0-safe) 2) route ARC to dedicated-pool-9 (capacity w/ larger RAM) 3) bump KV cache TTL and enable aggressive prefix caching. acct_omar: heads-up — letting ARC account team know, preparing customer comms. cs_maya: I'm on a call with Arcadia ops, they're seeing 5-10% user failures. We'll tell them short mitigation window and ask for traffic quiesce if needed. platform_dev_li: I can flip routing policy, give me thumbs. runtime_dev_jay: command to pin model (run on control plane): ```
POST /v1/tenants/arcadia/pin
{ "model": "arcadia-base-2.0-safe", "reason": "auto-fallback during prod degradation" }
``` platform_dev_li: executing route change now: `rbacctl route set --tenant arcadia --pool dedicated-pool-9 --priority high` platform_dev_li: applied. runtime_dev_jay: initiating safe variant pin via API. runtime_dev_jay: pin accepted, starting canary traffic to safe variant (10%). oncall_elena: enabling canary hold for 3m then ramp. ml_lead_sam: safe variant has lower context, quantized kernels; expect lower tail mem. ops_shift_lead: Arcadia ops confirms they can throttle some requests for 10m. cs_maya: Arcadia is asking for ETA on full mitigation. acct_omar: tell them 15-30m for full cutover; we'll update in 5 mins. runtime_dev_jay: rolling canary to 50% now. monitoring: error rate dropping to 2.3%. oncall_elena: good sign. runtime_dev_jay: ramping to 100%. platform_dev_li: full routing in place. monitoring: 95th latency down to 1.1s, errors <0.5%. cs_maya: Arcadia reported immediate improvement, sending one-line note: "recovering, thanks" :white_check_mark:. acct_omar: sending official incident note and will schedule post-incident call. security_tess: any chance this was triggered by malformed requests/exploit? logs so far show normal payloads, but I'll run sampling. security_tess: running sample check: no suspicious auth patterns. ml_lead_sam: opening a follow-up ticket to analyze tokenization failure modes and adjust model preprocessing. runtime_dev_jay: root cause hypothesis: large context threads bypassed prefix caching due to an edge of cache key mismatch after an internal change last week. when kv miss occurred, runtime attempted larger allocations, pushing some replicas to OOM-throttle and causing 5xx errors. runtime_dev_jay: mitigation steps we performed: pinned safe variant, routed to larger pool, bumped cache TTL & fixed cache-keying hotpatch will be rolled later. platform_dev_li: I'll keep route pinned for 2 hours then revert if stable. ops_shift_lead: oncall to monitor for next 2 hours, ops on call for Arcadia will be paged for regressions. cs_maya: Arcadia wants timeline for permanent fix. acct_omar: commit to RCA doc by EOD and a scheduled remediation plan with timelines tomorrow. runtime_dev_jay: creating incident tracker: INC-ARC-4123456789. ml_lead_sam: also recommending model QA to include long-context fuzzing. security_tess: all good on security side. oncall_elena: thanks team — major props for fast coordination. oncall_elena: closing pager but keeping channel open for 2h watch. incident_bot: Incident marked P1 -> mitigated; watch mode enabled. oncall_elena: final note: postmortem owner assigned to runtime_dev_jay. cs_maya: will follow up with customer sync. acct_omar: sending billing/credits note per SLA. runtime_dev_jay: follow-up action items: 1) hotpatch cache-key fix (PR opened) 2) schedule controlled rollout of safe variant changes 3) add long-context tests 4) update runbooks for tenant-specific pin + route ops. ops_shift_lead: I'll add runbook updates to oncall playbook. oncall_elena: thanks, closing thread in 2h if no regressions.
